title: Corporate Advances of Delinquent Property Taxes and Insurance under Property Charge Advance Repayment
content:
Cedarline advances only the charge types the Property Charge Advance Repayment product lists as advanced charges, and only when the bill is past its due date unpaid and no set-aside on the loan pays it in full; a bill a Fully Funded LESA or Summit reserve can pay is paid from the set-aside instead, and only a set-aside shortfall left unpaid by the borrower is advanced, as the product's set-aside shortfall term provides. Delinquent homeowners-association dues are never advanced, as the product's association-dues term provides, and remain a matter between the borrower and the association. An advance is recorded only while the arrangement record is in notice period, pending signature, active or defaulted status. Each bill is advanced at most once, identified by its bill reference, and the borrower is notified within the product's advance notice period in calendar days; the advance is added to the loan balance on its payment date. A new advance during an active installment arrangement is added to the arrearage and, where the product provides that a new advance is added and the installment recomputed, the installment is recomputed over the remaining installments.

## Conditions for recording an advance

| Condition for recording an advance |
|---|
| The charge is one of the advanced charge types |
| The bill is past its due date and unpaid |
| No set-aside on the loan pays it in full; where a Fully Funded LESA or Summit reserve can pay it, it is paid from the set-aside instead |
| The arrangement record is in notice period, pending signature, active or defaulted status |
| The bill, identified by its bill reference, has not already been advanced |

The arrangement record's status and the advances already on the record are read from the system's records before the advance is recorded.

## What an advance does

- It raises the arrearage on the arrangement record by the amount advanced.
- It is added to the loan balance on its payment date.
- The borrower is notified of it within the advance notice period.
- During an active installment arrangement, it is added to the arrearage, and where recomputation applies the installment is recomputed over the remaining installments.

### Hypothetical cases

1. A hazard insurance premium is past due and unpaid, the loan has no set-aside, the record is pending signature, and the bill reference has not been advanced before: the bill is advanced once and added to the record.
2. The same bill reference is presented a second time: it is not advanced again.
3. A homeowners-association assessment is past due: it is not advanced.

The cases are illustrations only.
